nav.label: Main
nav.note: Lockstep opens your programs with the services they need, and closes what they leave behind.

apps.title: Apps
apps.subtitle: Open these through Lockstep's shortcut: their services start first, and what they leave running closes after them.

unsupported.title: Lockstep works on Windows
unsupported.body: This window is a preview; it cannot start, stop or close anything here.

folder.title: Choose the folder a program is installed in
folder.body: Everything that runs from there, and the services whose programs live there, belong to it.

program.title: Choose the program to open
program.body: Lockstep lists the programs in the folder, the likely one first.

shortcut.title: Open it from Lockstep's shortcut
shortcut.body: Its services start first, then the program. Windows asks once for permission to start and stop them.

close.title: Close it as usual
close.body: After a short wait, Lockstep closes the helpers it left running and stops its services.

app.removedServicesLeft: {name} was removed. Its services keep the settings Lockstep gave them, because Windows did not get permission to put them back.

removeConfirm.title: Remove {name}?
removeConfirm.body: Lockstep's shortcuts for {name} are deleted and the program's own shortcuts come back. The program itself stays installed.
removeConfirm.services: Windows asks once for permission to put its services back the way they were.

status.title: Now
status.idle: Not open. Its shortcut opens it with Lockstep.
status.idleLeftovers: Not open, but {programs} of its programs and {services} of its services are still running.
status.closing: {name} closed. Lockstep closes the rest in {time}, unless you open it again.

services.title: Services
services.subtitle: Started before {name} opens and stopped after it closes.
services.none: No services. Add one if the program needs it.

programs.title: Programs
programs.closeAll: Close programs left running from its folders
programs.closeAllHint: Each one is asked to close first and ended only if it does not.
programs.seenEmpty: Programs show up here after {name} has been open once.

folders.title: Folders
folders.subtitle: Programs and services in these folders belong to {name}.

timing.title: Timing
timing.waitHint: Opening it again during the wait keeps everything running.
timing.delayHint: Some services say they are running before they answer; a few seconds give them time.

permission.why: Windows lets only administrators start and stop services. Lockstep asks once, then starts and stops these for you without asking again.
permission.granted: Lockstep may now start and stop its services.
permission.declined: Windows did not get permission. Lockstep cannot start or stop these services yet.

failed.one: {count} service could not be changed; see History.
failed.other: {count} services could not be changed; see History.

cleanup.title: Close what {name} left?
cleanup.intro: Programs get {seconds} seconds to close on their own before they are ended.
cleanup.whileOpen: The app is open; closing its programs closes it too.

skip.otherUser: Runs for another person on this computer
skip.serviceProcess: Runs the {name} service, which the app does not stop

add.title: Add an app
add.subtitle: Four steps; nothing changes on your computer until you save.

folder.title: Where is the program installed?
folder.body: Choose its own folder, such as C:\Program Files (x86)\National Instruments. Everything that runs from it belongs to the app.
folder.pick: The folder the program is installed in
folder.cannot: This folder cannot be an app's folder
folder.noProgramsBody: Choose the folder the program's .exe file is in, or one above it.

program.title: Which program should the shortcut open?
program.body: The likely one is first. Updaters and uninstallers are hidden.
program.name: Name
program.nameHint: The shortcut and Lockstep use this name.
program.argsHint: Passed to the program when it opens.

services.title: Which services come and go with it?
services.body: These look like {name}'s: their programs are in its folders or come from the same publisher.
services.failed: The services could not be read
services.none: No services look like the app's. You can add one.

manual.one: Start {count} of them only when needed
manual.other: Start {count} of them only when needed

services.manualHint: They start with Windows now. Set to start by hand, they run only while the app does.
services.vendorHint: Count these as part of the app too. Leave them out if they hold other programs you use on their own.

finish.title: Shortcut and timing
finish.replace: Put Lockstep's shortcut in place of "{file}" on the desktop
finish.publicBody: It opens the program without Lockstep. Delete it if you want only one.
finish.permissionBody: Lockstep needs an administrator's permission to start and stop these services. After that it does not ask again.

add.savedDesktop: {name} is ready. Open it with the new shortcut on your desktop.
add.savedNoPermission: {name} is saved, but Windows did not get permission for its services. You can give it on the app's page.

savedProblems.one: {name} is saved; {count} thing did not work, see the app's page.
savedProblems.other: {name} is saved; {count} things did not work, see the app's page.

problem.notAbsolute: Choose a folder on a drive, like C:\Program Files\Vendor.
problem.driveRoot: A whole drive holds too much: choose the program's own folder.
problem.system: Windows' own folders cannot be used.
problem.tooBroad: This folder holds many unrelated programs: choose the program's own folder inside it.

history.title: History
history.subtitle: Every time an app closed: what started, what stopped, and what did not work.

empty.title: Nothing yet
empty.body: Each time an app closes, what Lockstep did shows up here.

clearConfirm.title: Clear the history?
clearConfirm.body: The list of what Lockstep did is deleted. Apps and their settings stay.

problem.access_denied: Windows did not allow it (it runs as administrator or another account)
problem.in_use: left running because {detail} is open and uses it
problem.service_process: left running because it runs the {detail} service
problem.other_user: runs for another person on this computer
problem.missing: this service is not on this computer any more
problem.shortcut_failed: the shortcut could not be made: {detail}
problem.shortcut_not_restored: the original shortcut could not be put back; it is in {detail}

settings.title: Settings
settings.waitHint: Each app can have its own wait. Opening it again during the wait keeps everything running.
settings.polite: Time a program gets to close on its own
settings.notifyHint: A Windows notification says what was stopped and closed.
settings.watchAlways: Also watch apps opened another way
settings.watchHint: Start menu, a file, the taskbar: Lockstep notices and closes what they leave too. It then starts with Windows and stays in the tray.

about.title: About
about.body: Lockstep grew out of two launcher scripts, for Ansys Electronics Desktop and Multisim, and does the same for any program. MIT license.

status.demoHint: This page runs in a browser with made-up apps; it changes nothing.

errors.invalid: Something is missing or not valid: {detail}
errors.not_found: That app is not there any more.
errors.shortcut_failed: The shortcut could not be made: {detail}
